headline: Vendor the framework from a verified published package
summary: The vendored framework arrived by way of a shallow clone, which checks nothing about what it fetched. It now comes from the published package and its bytes are verified against the registry's advertised digest before anything is unpacked.

items.title: The vendored framework is verified against a published digest
items.body: It was previously fetched with a shallow clone of a release tag, which trusts whatever that tag resolves to at the moment of the fetch and leaves no way to tell afterwards whether the tree matches anything upstream published. The bytes are now checked against the registry's advertised SHA-512 before being unpacked, the run stops rather than vendoring on a mismatch, and that digest is recorded alongside the version so the tree stays traceable to a specific published artifact. End-of-line handling is pinned for the vendored tree as part of this, since a checkout that rewrites line endings would leave the recorded digest describing something other than what is on disk.

items.title: The image no longer carries the framework's test and example trees
items.body: The published package contains only what actually runs, so the repository's test, example, documentation, benchmark and fuzzing trees are no longer vendored or shipped. Roughly a thousand files leave the image. Nothing that HermitStash calls is affected — the framework surface is unchanged.
